doc.title: Charles Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]

title: What music means and Art Blakey's line
summary: Music is something people need daily; Tolliver repeats Blakey's remark about washing away the dust of everyday life.

bands.name: Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: All right. Words of wisdom. I’m going to wrap up here with a question that I’ve been debating about asking. And I have two variations on it. So I’m going to try it out on you, Charles, what does music mean? Or what can music mean?

Well I think that music, you were talking about spiritual at the beginning, music in whatever form it is to people around the world, whether they know it or not, but most of them do, that they have to have it at some point during the day you know, in order to get
through you know with life as a human being on this planet. And as I said in the previous session we did, you know Art Blakey said it best — you know what he said? Right?
I’d like to hear it again.

Well yeah, I mean he’d come off of a blistering song and say to the audience, “Thank you very much ladies and gentlemen” and that featured so-and-so, “and we are here to wash away the dust of your everyday life.” And so that’s it.
